original_test_intent: Measure sequential write bandwidth and IOPS on the approved Windows storage target using CrystalDiskMark and compare the displayed result with the project specification.
original_method: A qualified Windows operator records platform/device/CrystalDiskMark identity, selects the approved disposable target or safe test-file scope and sequential-write profile, runs the GUI once, exports or screenshots the full result table, records health/events and leaves cleanup to the data owner.
manual_activity: Qualified operator controls the Windows GUI, verifies the designated disposable target/test-file scope, runs only the approved sequential-write profile and captures evidence.
required_inputs: Approved Windows SUT and CrystalDiskMark version/checksum
Exact storage model/serial/firmware/drive letter and disposable target or safe test-file scope
Sequential-write profile, test size/count, cache/power policy and duration
Versioned write bandwidth/IOPS thresholds with units/tolerance
Data-loss authorization, health/thermal abort and cleanup policy
safety_requirements: Verify drive identity and write scope before GUI Start
Do not run default full suite or write to OS/production/in-use storage unless explicitly approved
Stop on wrong drive/profile, unexpected scope, device/thermal error or instability
No automatic retry, formatting, deletion or restoration
agent_execution_scope: Review operator-supplied version, target, profile, screenshot/export and health evidence
Compare recorded metrics with supplied thresholds without claiming GUI control
Do not operate the GUI, infer clicks, fabricate visual results or issue DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Provide target, profile, threshold and write authorization
Ensure qualified operator executes GUI and captures evidence
Review result/health evidence and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects SSH execution, but a GUI limitation alone does not define target safety, profile reproducibility or complete evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: MANUAL ONLY: operator runs the approved CrystalDiskMark sequential-write item on the exact designated Windows target and saves the unmodified result table.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Sequential write, bandwidth/IOPS, Windows CrystalDiskMark and 20/30 planning fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an approved CrystalDiskMark build and signed operator checklist binding drive serial, profile, size/count and thresholds to screenshot/export evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe write scope, reproducibility, target identity, health checks and cleanup without replacing the GUI.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A CLI or other benchmark cannot be substituted without separately approved equivalence; the GUI sequential-write result remains required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Caching, filesystem/test-file behavior, free space, drive conditioning and thermal state affect displayed values.

project_override_considerations: Project-specific CrystalDiskMark settings and specification are readiness inputs; they must not be invented or silently replaced with another tool or default full-suite settings.
expected_evidence: Operator/date plus Windows and CrystalDiskMark version identity
Exact target model/serial/firmware/drive letter and approved write/test-file scope
Sequential-write profile, test size/count and unmodified screenshot/export
Displayed write MB/s and IOPS mapped to versioned thresholds
Pre/post health, temperature and Windows event/device errors
GUI exit, no unintended process and owner-directed cleanup

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Windows CrystalDiskMark procedure and spec-comparison criterion are semantically aligned. Missing target, profile and numeric thresholds are project readiness inputs, not contradictory source statements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A qualified Windows operator can perform the GUI test once the target, profile and specification are supplied; the agent limitation makes it MANUAL ONLY rather than inherently blocked.

review_improvement: Preserves the manual GUI boundary while making destructive write scope, exact profile and trustworthy evidence explicit.
independent_technical_reasoning: Sequential write modifies the selected test file or volume and its result depends on transfer size, queue/thread profile, caching and drive state. Those selections are visible only in the GUI evidence, so an SSH agent cannot recreate or attest the run. Target identity and an unmodified result table are essential to both safety and comparability.
